question: Identify the normal forms used in relational database normalization.
Given a relational table containing repeated student and course information, normalize it into Third Normal Form (3NF).
Examine a relational database schema and identify the functional dependencies and anomalies that normalization should address.
A university proposes storing student and course information in a single denormalized table. Assess this design in terms of data redundancy and integrity.
Develop a normalized relational database schema for a university registration system that minimizes redundancy and maintains data integrity.
List the major levels of software testing used during software development.
Explain how different levels of software testing contribute to functional correctness, security, and reliability in an online banking application.
Given the requirements of an online banking application, classify suitable testing techniques for verifying functional correctness, security, and reliability.

Examine a testing strategy for an online banking application that consists only of unit tests and manual user-acceptance testing, and identify gaps in its coverage of functional correctness, security, and reliability.

A team proposes to test an online banking application using automated functional regression tests and a single penetration test before release. Assess whether this strategy adequately ensures functional correctness, security, and reliability, and justify your judgement against each of the three requirements.
State the conditions that determine whether a resource allocation state is safe.
Explain how the Banker's algorithm uses available resources and maximum process requirements to prevent unsafe allocation.
Examine the allocation, maximum demand, and available resource matrices to identify the processes that can complete in a safe sequence.
Given a resource allocation state and a pending resource request, justify whether granting the request would preserve system safety.
Develop a resource allocation procedure based on the Banker's algorithm that checks system safety before granting process requests.
Explain how the Arithmetic Logic Unit (ALU) performs arithmetic and logical operations during instruction execution.
Given two binary operands, execute specified addition, subtraction, AND, and OR operations using the ALU.
Trace an instruction's execution and distinguish the roles of the ALU, registers, and control signals in producing its result.

A processor's instruction set requires addition, subtraction, AND, OR, and comparison. Assess whether an ALU that implements only addition, AND, OR, and NOT can support every required operation, justifying how each missing operation could or could not be realized from the available ones.
Design a basic ALU that supports binary addition, subtraction, AND, OR, and comparison operations.
State the best-case and worst-case time complexities of binary search.
Explain why binary search reduces the search space by half after each comparison.
Use binary search to locate a specified element in a sorted array and show the sequence of comparisons.
A developer proposes using binary search on an unsorted array. Assess whether this approach is valid and justify your decision based on the algorithm's requirements.
Develop an iterative binary search algorithm that returns the position of a target element in a sorted array.
Identify the components used to calculate an effective address in base and offset addressing.
Explain how the base register and offset value are combined to determine an operand's effective address.
Given several memory access instructions, distinguish how base addressing and offset addressing determine their effective addresses.
Assess whether base and offset addressing provide an appropriate method for accessing elements of an array stored in memory.
Construct a sequence of assembly instructions that uses base and offset addressing to access successive elements of an array.
Identify the key components used in symmetric and asymmetric encryption.
Explain how symmetric and asymmetric encryption protect confidential academic records through different key-management mechanisms.
Given an academic records system, demonstrate how symmetric encryption can be used to encrypt a confidential student record.
Compare the key distribution process and encryption workflow of symmetric and asymmetric encryption when protecting academic records.
Design an encryption architecture for an academic records system that uses symmetric and asymmetric encryption to protect stored and transmitted records.
State the four ACID properties of database transactions.
Given two concurrent transactions that update the same account balance, construct a serial schedule that preserves database consistency.
Examine a concurrent transaction schedule and identify whether it contains a lost update, dirty read, or inconsistent retrieval.
Assess whether strict two-phase locking is appropriate for preventing concurrency anomalies in a university registration database.
Develop a transaction scheduling strategy for a university registration system that maintains consistency during simultaneous student registrations.
Define coupling and cohesion in software module design.
Explain why high cohesion and low coupling generally improve software maintainability.

Apply the coupling classification (data, stamp, control, common, and content coupling) to determine the type of coupling between two modules when one module passes a flag that selects which operation the other module performs.
A software system contains modules with extensive dependencies and unrelated responsibilities. Assess which design improvements should be prioritized to improve maintainability.

Redesign a software system in which a single module handles user input, database access, and report formatting into cohesive modules with minimal coupling, specifying each module's responsibility and interface while preserving the existing functionality.
State the operations supported by the stack data structure and identify its underlying principle.
Explain how the Last-In, First-Out (LIFO) principle determines the order of stack operations.
Trace a sequence of push and pop operations and identify the resulting stack contents and the position of the top element after each operation.
Assess whether an array-based stack is suitable for an application requiring frequent insertions with unpredictable storage requirements.
Develop an array-based stack implementation that supports push, pop, peek, and overflow and underflow detection.
Identify the main types of DNS servers involved in domain name resolution.
Given a domain name and a DNS lookup scenario, trace the resolution process to determine the IP address returned to the client.
Examine a DNS resolution failure and distinguish whether the problem originates from the local cache, recursive resolver, or authoritative name server.
Assess whether relying exclusively on a single DNS server is appropriate for a university network that requires high availability.
Design a hierarchical DNS architecture for a university network that supports internal domain resolution, redundancy, and reliable external access.
State the definitions of clustered and non-clustered indexes.
Explain how clustered and non-clustered indexes organize and locate records in a relational database.
Given a database table and a frequently executed range query, select an appropriate index type for the query.
A database administrator proposes creating several indexes on a table that frequently handles insertions and range queries. Assess the proposal in terms of retrieval performance and update overhead.
Design an indexing strategy for a university database that supports efficient student searches and course registration queries.
List the five stages of a basic instruction pipeline.
Given a sequence of instructions and a five-stage pipeline, calculate the number of clock cycles required to complete their execution without hazards.
Examine an instruction sequence and identify data, control, and structural hazards that may interrupt pipeline execution.
Assess whether forwarding or pipeline stalling is a more suitable solution for resolving data hazards in a given processor workload.
Design a five-stage instruction pipeline that incorporates forwarding and hazard detection to improve instruction throughput.
List the core principles of the Agile software development approach.
Explain how iterative development and continuous customer feedback support projects with changing requirements.
Given a software project with frequently changing requirements, organize its development activities into iterative Agile sprints.
Examine a project scenario and identify how changing requirements affect sprint planning, product backlog management, and team coordination.
Develop an Agile project management plan that incorporates sprint cycles, backlog refinement, and continuous stakeholder feedback.
Identify the main components of an access control policy.
Explain how authentication, authorization, and role-based permissions restrict access to university information.
Given student, faculty, and administrator roles, assign appropriate permissions for viewing and modifying academic records.
Examine an existing university access control policy and identify excessive permissions and potential privilege escalation paths.
Assess whether a role-based access control model provides sufficient protection for student and faculty records while supporting legitimate academic activities.
State the best-case, average-case, and worst-case time complexities of merge sort and insertion sort.
Explain how the divide-and-conquer strategy enables merge sort to achieve its time complexity.
Given an input array, execute merge sort and insertion sort to determine the sorted output.
For a small, nearly sorted dataset, justify whether insertion sort or merge sort is the more appropriate sorting algorithm.
Develop a hybrid sorting algorithm that combines insertion sort and merge sort to improve performance on datasets containing small subarrays.
State the relationship between subnet masks, network addresses, and host addresses in IPv4 subnetting.
Explain how subnetting divides a larger IP network into smaller logical networks.
Examine a subnet allocation plan and identify address wastage, overlapping address ranges, and insufficient host capacity.

A network administrator proposes allocating equal-sized /26 subnets to every department of a university network whose departments have widely different host requirements. Assess whether this allocation is appropriate, considering host capacity and address wastage.
Construct a Variable Length Subnet Masking (VLSM) plan for a university network with different host requirements for its departments.
Define precision, recall, and F1-score in classification evaluation.
Explain how false positives and false negatives influence precision and recall.
Given a confusion matrix, calculate the precision, recall, and F1-score of a classification model.
Examine the evaluation results of two classification models and identify how their false-positive and false-negative rates differ.
Develop an evaluation procedure that compares classification models using precision, recall, F1-score, and confusion matrices.
List the four necessary conditions for deadlock to occur.
Given a resource allocation graph, determine whether a deadlock exists among the processes.
Examine a resource allocation graph and trace how circular wait and resource dependency can lead to deadlock.
A system uses resource ordering to prevent deadlock. Assess the effectiveness of this approach and identify its possible limitations.
Develop a deadlock prevention strategy for an operating system that manages multiple processes competing for limited resources.
List the major phases of a compiler in their execution order.
Explain how lexical, syntax, and semantic analysis transform source code into an intermediate representation.
Given a source-code statement, identify its tokens, construct its syntax structure, and check for basic semantic errors.

Assess whether a compiler front end that performs type checking only after intermediate-code generation adequately detects lexical, syntax, and semantic errors before code generation, and justify the consequences of this ordering.
Design a simplified compiler front end that performs lexical analysis, syntax analysis, and semantic checking for arithmetic expressions.
Define a deterministic finite automaton and identify its five formal components.
Explain how DFA states represent the progress of recognizing a required pattern in an input string.
Given a DFA that recognizes binary strings ending with 01, trace its state transitions for the input string 1101.
Examine a DFA transition table and identify the states and transitions responsible for accepting strings ending with 01.

A proposed DFA over {0,1} has start state q0, accepting state q2, and transitions q0–0→q1, q0–1→q0, q1–0→q1, q1–1→q2, q2–0→q0, and q2–1→q0. Assess whether it accepts every binary string ending with 01 and rejects all others, justifying your conclusion with a test string.
State the homogeneous transformation matrices used for two-dimensional translation and rotation.
Explain how homogeneous coordinates represent translation and rotation as matrix operations.
Examine two sequences of geometric transformations and determine how changing their order affects the final position of an object.

To rotate a square by 90° about its centre (2, 2), one student applies T(2, 2)·R(90°)·T(−2, −2) and another applies R(90°)·T(−2, −2)·T(2, 2), where the rightmost matrix acts first. Determine which sequence produces the required result and justify the selection using the order of matrix multiplication.
Develop a sequence of homogeneous transformation matrices that rotates an object around an arbitrary pivot point and then translates it to a specified position.
Identify the major types of data replication used in distributed databases.
Explain how maintaining multiple copies of data helps a distributed database remain available during server failures.
Given a distributed database with three replicas, determine which replicas can continue serving read requests after one replica becomes unavailable.
Examine a distributed database architecture and identify how replica failures, network partitions, and synchronization delays affect data availability and consistency.
Design a replication architecture for a distributed database that maintains service availability during individual server failures.
List the fundamental usability principles used in interface design.
Explain how consistency, feedback, and error prevention improve the usability of a student registration interface.
Given a student registration interface, identify design changes that would improve navigation, feedback, and error prevention.
Assess a university registration interface using usability principles and justify which design problems should be addressed first.
Develop a redesigned student registration interface that incorporates consistency, clear feedback, accessibility, and error prevention.
Identify the cryptographic keys and hash functions involved in generating and verifying a digital signature.
Given a message and the sender's private key, demonstrate the steps required to generate a digital signature and verify it using the corresponding public key.
Examine a digital signature verification process and identify how message modification or an incorrect public key affects verification.
Assess whether digital signatures alone provide sufficient protection for confidential electronic communication, considering authentication, integrity, and confidentiality.
Design a digital document verification workflow that uses digital signatures to establish authenticity and detect unauthorized modifications.
Identify the main hardware components required for an embedded temperature monitoring system.
Explain how a microcontroller processes sensor readings and controls an alarm based on a predefined temperature threshold.
Given sensor readings and a specified temperature threshold, determine when the embedded system should activate its alarm.
Examine the operation of a temperature monitoring system and identify possible causes of incorrect alarm activation or missed threshold violations.

Assess whether sampling the temperature sensor once every 60 seconds is suitable for an embedded monitoring system in which the temperature can rise past the alarm threshold within 10 seconds, justifying your decision in terms of detection delay.
Identify the three common cache mapping techniques used in computer architecture.
Explain how direct, fully associative, and set-associative cache mapping determine where memory blocks are stored.
Given a memory address and cache configuration, determine the cache set and block location using direct mapping.
A processor experiences frequent conflict misses with direct-mapped caching. Assess whether set-associative mapping would be a suitable improvement.
Design a cache configuration for a processor workload that balances hit rate, hardware complexity, and access time.
Define the critical path and identify the meaning of activity slack in project scheduling.
Explain how task dependencies and activity durations determine the critical path of a software project.
Given a project activity network with task durations and dependencies, calculate the critical path and total project completion time.
Examine a software project network and identify how delays in critical and non-critical activities affect the overall schedule.
Develop a project schedule for a software development project using activity dependencies, estimated durations, and critical path analysis.
Identify the main components involved in offline data storage and synchronization in a mobile application.
Explain how local storage and synchronization mechanisms allow a mobile application to operate without continuous network connectivity.
Given a mobile application with cached records, determine how locally modified data should be synchronized after network connectivity returns.
Examine an offline synchronization scenario and identify potential data conflicts when the same record is modified on multiple devices.
Assess whether a last-write-wins synchronization strategy is suitable for a mobile application in which users frequently modify shared records.
Define Term Frequency-Inverse Document Frequency (TF-IDF) and word embeddings.
Explain how TF-IDF and word embeddings represent textual information for machine learning models.
Given a collection of academic documents, generate TF-IDF feature vectors for use in a text classification model.
Examine the feature representations produced by TF-IDF and word embeddings and identify how each captures word importance and semantic relationships.
Develop a text classification pipeline that compares TF-IDF and word embedding representations using the same training and evaluation dataset.
State Ohm's law and identify the SI units of voltage, current, and resistance.
Explain how changes in resistance affect current when the applied voltage remains constant.
A 12 V DC source is connected to a 4 Ω resistor. Calculate the current flowing through the resistor.
A circuit designer proposes replacing a 4 Ω resistor with an 8 Ω resistor while maintaining the same supply voltage. Assess the effect on current consumption and justify the decision.
Design a DC resistive circuit that draws a specified current from a fixed voltage source using appropriate resistor values.
Identify the principal components of reinforced concrete and state their structural functions.
Explain how concrete and steel reinforcement work together to resist compressive and tensile stresses.
Given the dimensions and material properties of a reinforced concrete beam, calculate its nominal bending capacity using the specified design equation.
Examine the loading conditions of a reinforced concrete column and identify the effects of axial load and bending moment on its structural behaviour.
Develop a preliminary reinforced concrete structural design for a high-rise building that accounts for the specified loading conditions.
State the first law of thermodynamics for a closed system.
Explain how heat transfer, work transfer, and internal energy change are related in a closed thermodynamic system.
Examine the energy interactions during a closed-system process and distinguish heat supplied, work performed, and changes in internal energy.

A student reports that a closed system which receives 50 kJ of heat while doing 70 kJ of work on its surroundings has an internal-energy increase of 20 kJ. Assess whether this energy balance is physically consistent with the first law of thermodynamics.

Design a closed-system process sequence, with heat and work interactions of your choice, that returns the system to its initial state, and formulate the first-law energy balance for each process and for the complete cycle.
State Newton's second law of motion and write its mathematical expression.
A 5 kg object experiences a net force of 20 N. Calculate its acceleration.
Examine the forces acting on an object moving along an inclined plane and determine how each force contributes to its net acceleration.

For a box pulled at constant velocity across a rough floor, one student's free-body diagram shows the applied horizontal force larger than friction, while another student's shows the two forces equal in magnitude. Determine which diagram correctly represents the forces and justify your selection using Newton's second law.
Develop an experimental procedure to investigate the relationship between applied force, mass, and acceleration using a laboratory trolley.
Define reaction rate and identify two factors that influence it.
Explain how increasing temperature affects the frequency and energy of effective molecular collisions.
Given experimental concentration and reaction-rate data, calculate the average reaction rate over a specified time interval.
A researcher proposes increasing temperature rather than reactant concentration to accelerate a chemical reaction. Assess this proposal using collision theory and the experimental conditions.
Design a controlled laboratory experiment to investigate how temperature affects the rate of a chemical reaction while keeping other variables constant.
Define natural selection and identify the role of heritable variation in evolution.
Given a population with different inherited traits and survival rates, predict how the frequency of a particular trait may change over several generations.
Examine population data across multiple generations and identify evidence that differential survival and reproduction have influenced trait frequencies.
Assess whether an observed change in a population's trait frequency provides sufficient evidence for natural selection rather than genetic drift.
Develop a controlled investigation to test how an environmental change influences natural selection in a population of organisms.
Define interest rate, investment expenditure, and aggregate demand.
Explain how an increase in interest rates can influence borrowing costs, business investment, and aggregate demand.
Given an economic scenario involving an increase in interest rates, identify the likely direction of change in investment expenditure and aggregate demand.
Examine the transmission mechanism through which changes in interest rates affect household consumption, business investment, and overall economic output.
Develop a monetary policy proposal for managing inflation through interest rate adjustments while considering the effects on investment and aggregate demand.
Define the null hypothesis, alternative hypothesis, significance level, and p-value.
Explain how the significance level and p-value are used to make decisions in statistical hypothesis testing.
Examine a hypothesis-testing result and distinguish the evidence provided by the test statistic, p-value, and confidence interval.
A researcher rejects the null hypothesis at a 5% significance level. Assess whether this result establishes practical significance as well as statistical significance.
Formulate a hypothesis-testing procedure to investigate whether the average examination score of a university student population differs from a specified benchmark.
Identify the major categories of solid waste commonly generated on a university campus.
Explain how waste segregation and recycling reduce the environmental impacts of campus waste disposal.
Given a list of campus waste materials, classify each material into appropriate recycling, organic, and general waste categories.
Examine campus waste generation data and identify the departments and waste categories contributing most significantly to the total waste volume.
Assess whether a proposed campus recycling programme is likely to reduce landfill waste, considering participation rates, collection facilities, and operational costs.
Identify the common types of organizational structures used in business management.
Explain how hierarchical and decentralized organizational structures influence communication and managerial authority.
Given a company experiencing delayed decisions due to multiple management levels, identify an organizational structure that could improve decision-making.
Assess whether a decentralized organizational structure is appropriate for a company operating across several geographically distributed branches.
Develop an organizational structure for a growing company that supports effective communication, accountability, and timely decision-making.
State the fundamental accounting equation and identify its three components.
Explain why every business transaction must maintain the balance of the accounting equation.
Examine a series of business transactions and classify their effects on assets, liabilities, and owner's equity.
A company's recorded transactions result in an imbalance in its accounting equation. Assess the possible recording errors that could explain the discrepancy.
Develop a set of representative business transactions and prepare their corresponding accounting equation effects for a newly established business.
Define unconditioned stimulus, conditioned stimulus, unconditioned response, and conditioned response.
Given a learning scenario involving a repeated association between a sound and food, identify the conditioned stimulus and conditioned response.
Examine a behavioural conditioning experiment and distinguish the stages of acquisition, extinction, and spontaneous recovery.
Assess whether classical conditioning provides an adequate explanation for a complex human behaviour involving both environmental and cognitive influences.
Design an ethical behavioural experiment to investigate how repeated stimulus associations influence a specific learned response.
Identify common methods of formative assessment used in university courses.
Explain how continuous feedback and formative assessment help students identify learning gaps.
Given a university course with low student performance in weekly assessments, select appropriate formative assessment activities to address the identified learning gaps.
Examine student assessment records before and after formative feedback and identify patterns indicating changes in academic performance.
Develop a formative assessment plan for a university course that integrates quizzes, feedback, and progress monitoring throughout the semester.
Identify the major spatial and environmental considerations involved in university library planning.
Explain how natural lighting, circulation, and accessibility influence the functionality of a library layout.
Given a floor plan and building dimensions, allocate suitable spaces for reading areas, book storage, and circulation routes.

Examine a library floor plan in which the only entrance is reached by stairs and the main circulation route passes through the quiet reading area, and identify the conflicts it creates for accessibility, natural lighting, and movement.

A proposed university library layout places all reading areas in the windowless building core and the book stacks along the glazed perimeter. Assess whether this layout satisfies accessibility and natural-lighting requirements without compromising usable space.
Define heat exchanger effectiveness and identify the factors used to determine heat transfer performance.
Explain how the temperature difference between two fluids drives heat transfer in a heat exchanger.
Given the inlet and outlet temperatures and mass flow rates of two fluids, calculate the heat transfer rate of a heat exchanger.
Examine heat exchanger operating data and identify how changes in flow rate and inlet temperature influence its thermal performance.
Develop a heat exchanger configuration for a specified heating application that meets the required heat transfer capacity and operating constraints.
State the ratio test and comparison test for determining the convergence of an infinite series.
Explain how the ratio test distinguishes between convergent and divergent infinite series.
Use the ratio test to determine whether the series ∑_(n=1)^∞ n/(3^n) converges or diverges.
A student applies the ratio test to a series, obtains a limit equal to one, and concludes that the series converges. Assess whether the student's conclusion is justified by the ratio test.
Construct an infinite series that converges conditionally and justify its convergence using appropriate mathematical tests.
State Kirchhoff's Current Law and Kirchhoff's Voltage Law.
Explain how conservation of charge and conservation of energy form the basis of Kirchhoff's laws.
Examine a multi-loop circuit and formulate the independent current and voltage equations required to solve for unknown quantities.

For a three-loop circuit with four nodes, a student writes one KVL equation for every loop including the outer loop and one KCL equation for every node. Assess whether this set of equations is independent and sufficient to solve for the unknown currents, and justify your judgement.
Construct a multi-loop electrical circuit with specified resistor and voltage-source values, then formulate a complete system of Kirchhoff equations for its analysis.
Identify the purpose of an indicator, burette, pipette, and standard solution in acid-base titration.
Explain how the equivalence point and endpoint are used to determine the concentration of an unknown acid solution.
Given the volume and concentration of a standard base and the volume of an unknown acid, calculate the acid concentration using the balanced neutralization equation.
Examine titration readings from repeated trials and identify possible sources of systematic and random experimental errors.

Assess whether methyl orange is an appropriate indicator for determining the concentration of an unknown weak acid by titration with sodium hydroxide, considering the pH at the equivalence point and the indicator's transition range.
Write the standard expression for the resonant frequency of a series RLC circuit.
Interpret the physical significance of resonance in a series RLC circuit when inductive and capacitive reactances become equal.
For a series RLC circuit with L=0.2H and C=50μF, calculate its resonant frequency.
A designer proposes increasing capacitance to shift an RLC circuit toward a lower resonant frequency. Verify whether this design decision achieves the intended result.
Formulate a series RLC circuit specification that achieves a required resonant frequency using suitable inductance and capacitance values.
Identify the major fiscal policy instruments available to a government.
Interpret how government expenditure and taxation influence aggregate demand, employment, and the general price level.
Given an economy experiencing rising unemployment and moderate inflation, select an appropriate fiscal policy instrument and predict its immediate effect.
Distinguish the short-term employment effects of expansionary fiscal policy from its possible inflationary consequences.
Defend whether increasing public infrastructure expenditure is preferable to reducing income taxes when unemployment is high but inflationary pressure persists.
State the principle of moments and its mathematical representation.
Illustrate how moment equilibrium determines the support reactions of a statically determinate beam.
Decompose the loading conditions of a simply supported beam and establish the independent equilibrium equations required to determine its reactions.

For a 6 m simply supported beam carrying a 12 kN point load 2 m from support A, a student reports reactions R_A = 4 kN and R_B = 8 kN. Verify whether these reactions satisfy both vertical-force equilibrium and moment equilibrium, and justify your conclusion.
Formulate a loading configuration for a simply supported beam and construct the equilibrium equations needed to determine its support reactions.
Distinguish the definitions of correlation and causation.
Clarify why a statistical association between two variables does not necessarily establish a causal relationship.
A study finds a positive correlation between study hours and examination scores. Identify a potential confounding variable that should be considered.

A researcher concludes that increased screen time causes lower academic performance based only on a cross-sectional correlation. Challenge the validity of this conclusion using methodological reasoning.
Propose a research design that could investigate whether increased study time causes improvements in academic performance while controlling for potential confounding variables.
Identify common manufacturing processes used to produce precision mechanical components.
Summarize how machining, casting, and additive manufacturing differ in their production mechanisms.
A component requires a cylindrical shape with a specified surface finish and dimensional tolerance. Select a suitable manufacturing process.
Contrast the dimensional accuracy, material waste, and production limitations of CNC machining and additive manufacturing for a given component.
Devise a manufacturing process plan for producing a high-precision mechanical component within specified material and dimensional constraints.
State the product rule for differentiating two functions.
Interpret the product rule geometrically and explain how it relates to the rate of change of a product of functions.
Examine the argument (fg)′(x) = lim_(h→0) [f(x+h)g(x+h) − f(x)g(x)]/h = f′(x)g′(x) and locate the step where an incorrect differentiation assumption is introduced.

A student proves the product rule by adding and subtracting f(x+h)g(x) in the difference quotient and then taking limits, using the fact that a differentiable function is continuous. Assess whether the proof is valid by checking each assumption, intermediate step, and the conclusion.
Formulate a product rule for the derivative of three differentiable functions, f(x)g(x)h(x), and prove it using the two-function product rule.
Define administrative decentralization and identify its major forms.
Describe how transferring administrative authority to local governments can influence public service delivery.
Given a local government with limited authority over healthcare and education services, identify administrative responsibilities that could be decentralized.
Examine differences in service delivery between centralized and decentralized local administrations, considering accountability, funding, and resource distribution.
Formulate a decentralization framework for local public services that establishes administrative responsibilities, funding mechanisms, and accountability procedures.
Enumerate the major stages involved in conventional wastewater treatment.
Explain how primary and secondary treatment processes remove suspended solids and biodegradable organic matter.
Given wastewater characteristics and a treatment efficiency percentage, calculate the expected effluent concentration of an organic pollutant.
Diagnose a treatment plant's poor organic pollutant removal by examining its influent characteristics, aeration conditions, and biological treatment performance.
Justify whether an activated sludge process is appropriate for a wastewater treatment facility with variable organic loading and limited operating resources.
Recall the scheduling criteria used to measure CPU scheduling performance.
Explain why the order in which processes receive CPU time affects average waiting time.
Given a set of processes with arrival and burst times, calculate their average waiting time using Shortest Job First scheduling.
Compare the execution timelines of FCFS and SJF scheduling and identify how process burst-time variation affects waiting time.
Determine whether non-preemptive SJF is appropriate for an interactive operating system where process burst times are not known in advance.
State Le Chatelier's principle.
Predict the general direction in which a reversible reaction shifts when an external condition disturbs its equilibrium.
For the reaction N_2(g)+3H_2(g)⇌2NH_3(g), determine the direction of equilibrium shift when pressure is increased at constant temperature.
A chemical plant increases pressure to improve ammonia production. Judge whether this adjustment is sufficient to maximize production when temperature and operating costs are also considered.
Formulate an operating-condition strategy for an ammonia synthesis process that considers equilibrium yield, pressure, temperature, and energy requirements.
Identify the three fundamental components of constructive alignment in outcome-based education.
Interpret how course learning outcomes, teaching-learning activities, and assessment methods must align in an OBE framework.
Given a course learning outcome requiring students to analyze a database schema, select an assessment activity that measures the stated outcome.
Examine a course assessment plan and identify mismatches between its learning outcomes, teaching activities, and examination questions.

A course learning outcome requires students to design a normalized database schema, but the proposed assessment plan uses only a multiple-choice quiz on the definitions of normal forms. Appraise whether this plan provides sufficient evidence of achievement of the outcome, using constructive alignment as the criterion.
State the formula used to calculate the net present value of an investment project.
Explain why future cash flows are discounted when evaluating long-term investment decisions.
Examine the projected cash flows of an investment and distinguish the effects of initial cost, annual returns, and discount rate on its net present value.
A project has a positive net present value but involves substantial financial uncertainty. Defend whether the investment should be accepted using financial and risk considerations.
Construct a financial evaluation model for a proposed investment using projected cash flows, an appropriate discount rate, and net present value calculations.
Define social stratification and identify its major dimensions.
Explain how differences in income, social status, and educational resources can influence access to higher education.
Given enrolment statistics for students from different income groups, calculate the proportion of each group represented in a university cohort.
Interpret university enrolment data to identify patterns of educational inequality across socioeconomic groups.
Propose an institutional policy framework to reduce socioeconomic barriers to university admission and participation.
Identify the principal waves and intervals represented in a standard ECG waveform.
Given an ECG waveform with marked intervals, calculate the heart rate using the R-R interval.
Examine an ECG tracing and distinguish normal waveform components from deviations that may indicate an abnormal cardiac rhythm.
An ECG shows a regular rhythm with an R-R interval of 0.6 s, and the reader interprets it as sinus bradycardia. Assess whether this interpretation is supported by the recorded interval.
Develop a signal-processing workflow for detecting R peaks and estimating heart rate from a recorded ECG signal.
Identify the agricultural principles underlying crop rotation.
Explain how alternating crops with different nutrient requirements can influence soil fertility and pest populations.
Examine soil nutrient records and pest observations from successive growing seasons to identify the effects of a crop rotation pattern.
A farmer proposes repeating the same crop annually because of its high market value. Critique this decision in terms of soil nutrient depletion and pest management.
Formulate a multi-season crop rotation schedule for a farm that balances soil fertility, pest control, and crop productivity.
Identify the two fundamental principles of natural justice.
Explain how the right to a fair hearing and the rule against bias protect individuals during administrative proceedings.
Given a case in which an administrative authority imposes a penalty without hearing the affected individual, identify the relevant principle of natural justice.
Assess whether an administrative decision should be reconsidered when the affected party was denied an opportunity to respond to the allegations.
Draft a procedural framework for an administrative authority that incorporates fair hearing requirements and safeguards against decision-maker bias.
Identify the independent and dependent variables in a quantitative correlational study.
Explain how operational definitions and measurable indicators support the investigation of relationships between study habits and academic achievement.
Given a research objective concerning study habits and academic performance, formulate measurable indicators for both variables.

Examine a study design that correlates students' self-reported weekly study hours with their grade-point average, and identify potential confounding variables that could influence the relationship between study habits and academic achievement.
Critique whether a cross-sectional correlational design can adequately address a research question concerning the relationship between study habits and academic achievement.
State the pharmacokinetic relationship used to calculate a maintenance dose from drug clearance, target steady-state concentration, dosing interval, and bioavailability.
Interpret the relationship between drug clearance, dosing interval, bioavailability, and the maintenance dose required to sustain a steady-state plasma concentration.
Differentiate the effects of increased clearance and reduced bioavailability on the maintenance dose while keeping the target concentration and dosing interval constant.
Verify whether a proposed maintenance dose is appropriate for a patient by assessing the supplied clearance, bioavailability, dosing interval, and target concentration.
Formulate a maintenance-dosing regimen for a hypothetical patient using the supplied pharmacokinetic parameters and a specified target steady-state concentration.
Identify the major environmental factors that influence the stability of temperature-sensitive pharmaceutical formulations.
Interpret how temperature and storage duration influence the degradation of a temperature-sensitive pharmaceutical formulation.
Use the supplied degradation data to estimate the remaining drug concentration after a specified storage period under a given temperature condition.
Examine the degradation data to distinguish the effects of storage temperature and storage duration on the stability of the pharmaceutical formulation.
Develop a storage protocol for the temperature-sensitive formulation using its degradation characteristics and intended storage period.
Define overshoot, settling time, and stability in the transient response of a feedback control system.
